summary: Confusing 429 waves during dedicated-pool scale-up with ephemeral worker fallback
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent 429 "waves" observed shortly after our dedicated GPU pool autoscaler added capacity (scale-up). Pattern: a few minutes after scale-up the customer sees repeated 429s across many short-lived webhook callbacks/orchestrated workers. 429s subside after ~7–12 minutes.

Impact:
- AtlasMaps (dedicated) experienced degraded ingestion throughput for mapping telemetry; spike affected ~20% of requests for a 10-minute window and caused backfills to queue.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool (prod-us-west), autoscaled from 8->12 GPUs at 2026-03-10T14:22Z.
- Traffic: multiplexed signed-callbacks + ephemeral worker processes that create short-lived API keys.

Steps to reproduce (customer provided):
1) Kick off orchestrated ingestion with 80 concurrent short-lived worker processes (each worker performs many small webhook callbacks via signed URL).
2) Trigger a manual pool scale-up (or wait for autoscaler).
3) Observe increased rate of 429s for the next ~5–15 minutes, then recovery.

Observed behavior:
- 429 responses from rate-limiter service. Throttle headers inconsistent (X-RateLimit-Remaining shows small remaining count then jumps).
- Console shows tenant quota temporarily near 0 then replenishes.

Expected behavior:
- Scale-up should reduce contention and avoid tenant-level 429s for legitimate fanout workloads.

Attachments / Logs:
- Customer provided request id samples: req_az9f2, req_bv4k1, req_cx1m9 (timestamps 2026-03-10T14:25Z - 14:31Z).
- Grafana snapshot (customer): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ingest/atlasmaps-scaleup-spike

Notes: This looks similar to tenant-token-bucket drift but happens aligned with worker handoff during autoscaler activity. Customer is requesting guidance and a mitigation while we investigate root cause.
investigation_notes: SRE initial triage 2026-03-10: correlated time window with autoscaler event; autoscaler initiated host replacement on two nodes leading to short connection churn.
Hypothesis A: healthcheck/probe traffic or ephemeral worker registration counted against tenant burst budget causing transient depletion during handoff.
Hypothesis B: new hosts introduced slightly different rate-window offset, causing token refill epoch misalignment and sawtooth-like refill behavior for short-lived keys.
Ran quick checks: rate-limiter logs show simultaneous token debit events from multiple ephemeral keys at handoff time; many of these map to signed-callback origin IPs.
Related metric: tenant_token_window_drift_us spiked from ~30us baseline to 12ms during the event window.
Cross-reference: Slack thread #support-atlasmaps (https://slack.redwood.ai/#support/archives/C03XYZ) contains customer traces.
comments: Support (Maya): Acknowledged and requested customer sample ids and exact scale-up timestamp; asked for short-term workaround request.
Customer (AtlasMaps): Provided the three request ids and confirmed they can reproduce by triggering an ingestion job + scale-up. Asked for an immediate mitigation as backfill is blocked.
SRE (Ethan): Noted temporary mitigation available: exclude our internal healthcheck probes from tenant burst accounting and increase customer's burst pool delta for the next autoscaler window.

Engineering (Priya - rate-limiter): Looking at token-slicing and refill alignment code; flagged possible double-counting on signed URL callback handshake path. Will instrument extra logs for next hour.
Support (Maya): Communicated mitigation plan to customer and scheduled 30-minute maintenance window for config tweak.
temporary_workaround: Applied temporary config change at 2026-03-11T09:05Z: - increased AtlasMaps dedicated burst delta by 25% for 30 minutes around autoscaler events; added exclusion rule for internal healthcheck user-agent. Observed immediate reduction in 429 incidence in following test run.
resolution_notes:
Root cause (tentative): combination of (1) ephemeral worker fanout registering many short-lived API tokens during host handoff and (2) epoch-aligned token refill windows across new hosts created a short interval where token consumption outran the (global) refill accounting, causing tenant bucket depletion. Fixes rolled out:
- Short-term: keep the burst-delta increase for scheduled scale events and exclude known internal probes from tenant accounting.
- Mid-term (engineering): PR opened to add guard in rate-limiter to dedupe near-simultaneous debit events for token families created within 2s of each other (https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4123).
- Follow-up: add metric epi.ephemeral_worker_fanout and alert when >50k token creations/minute for a tenant during autoscaler events.

Post-action: Customer ran identical ingestion with scale-up on 2026-03-11T09:40Z and reported no 429s. Ticket resolved pending longer-term fix and postmortem doc.
next_steps: Engineering to land PR and roll canary to staging by 2026-03-18.
SRE to create a runbook entry for dedicated-pool scale events: recommend temporary burst-delta bump and probe exclusion during scheduled host replacements.
Support to follow up with AtlasMaps on 2026-03-15 to confirm no recurrence and coordinate postmortem share.
Observability: add epi.ephemeral_worker_fanout metric and a Grafana panel for tenant token-creation rate.
